original_question: Are there infinite-dimensional reflexive Banach spaces with property (D_1), meaning that every sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n: [0, 1] → X which is bounded in L^1([0, 1], X) and converges scalarly in measure to 0 has a subsequence that converges scalarly to 0 almost everywhere?
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, Problem 5.9 (Dilworth-Girardi): "Are there reflexive (infinite-dimensional) Banach spaces with property (D1)?" The property (D_p) is defined immediately above in the same subsection. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem, keeps the existential quantifier, keeps reflexivity and infinite dimensionality, fixes p=1, and paraphrases property (D1) essentially as the paper does: L^1-bounded strongly measurable functions on [0,1] that are scalarly null in measure should have a subsequence that is scalarly null almost everywhere. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: Make explicit that the paper works with real Banach spaces. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
Specify that [0,1] is equipped with the Lebesgue measure λ. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Spell out "converges scalarly in measure to 0": for every x* in X*, the scalar sequence x*∘f_n converges to 0 in measure. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Spell out "converges scalarly to 0 a.e.": there is a λ-null set E such that for every t in [0,1]\E and every x* in X*, x*(f_{n_k}(t)) tends to 0. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
Make the subsequence explicit as an index subsequence (f_{n_k}). ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, mention that L^1([0,1],X) is the Lebesgue-Bochner space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable X-valued functions. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional reflexive real Banach space X with property (D1), meaning that whenever (f_n) is a sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n:[0,1]→X with sup_n ||f_n||_{L^1([0,1],X)}<∞ and x*(f_n)→0 in measure on [0,1] for every x*∈X*, there is a subsequence (f_{n_k}) such that x*(f_{n_k}(t))→0 for λ-almost every t∈[0,1] and every x*∈X*? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Problem 5.9 in Section 5.3 of the paper. The subsection first defines property (D_p) for 1≤p≤∞ and then asks the p=1 existence question for reflexive infinite-dimensional spaces. Your draft already captures the right target; the needed refinements are only the paper's ambient conventions and the explicit meanings of scalar convergence in measure and scalar almost-everywhere convergence. It should not be broadened to Problem 5.8 or to other values of p. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
